title: Divergences
comment: Divergences — Csiszar divergences is a unifying way to define losses between arbitrary positive measures (discrete & densities). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-divergence

title: Step Size
comment: Step Size — "Greedy" gradient descent using optimal step choice at each iteration produces orthogonal successive directions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient_descent
alt_text: Step Size. "Greedy" gradient descent using optimal step choice at each iteration produces orthogonal successive directions.

title: Heat
comment: Heat — The heat can be applied to diffuse probability density (in particular, maintains positivity and unit mass). It corresponds to the distribution of a Brownian motion at time t. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation
alt_text: Heat. The heat can be applied to diffuse probability density (in particular, maintains positivity and unit mass). It corresponds to the distribution of a Brownian motion at time t.

title: Lloyd
comment: Lloyd — Loyds algorithm defines a segmentation of the domain using Voronoi cells. The associated dual graph is a Delaunay triangulation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd%27s_algorithm
alt_text: Lloyd. Loyds algorithm defines a segmentation of the domain using Voronoi cells. The associated dual graph is a Delaunay triangulation.

title: Harmonic
comment: Harmonic — Harmonic functions are obtained by solving Laplace equation and define interpolating functions when using Dirichlet boundary conditions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplace%27s_equation
alt_text: Harmonic. Harmonic functions are obtained by solving Laplace equation and define interpolating functions when using Dirichlet boundary conditions.

title: Fft
comment: Fft — The Fast Fourier and Wavelet transforms correspond to two sparse factorizations of an orthonormal matrix, leading to two fast iterative algorithms of O(n log(n)) and O(n) complexities. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Fourier_transform
alt_text: Fft. The Fast Fourier and Wavelet transforms correspond to two sparse factorizations of an orthonormal matrix, leading to two fast iterative algorithms of O(n log(n)) and O(n) complexities.

title: Pendulum
comment: Pendulum — The simple gravity pendulum is one of the simplest nonlinear second order ODE. Exhibits elliptic-shape orbits in phase space for small enough initial speeds. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pendulum_(mathematics
alt_text: Pendulum. The simple gravity pendulum is one of the simplest nonlinear second order ODE. Exhibits elliptic-shape orbits in phase space for small enough initial speeds.

title: Taylor Exp
comment: Taylor Exp — Taylor series approximate within its radius of convergence a function by a polynomial. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_series
alt_text: Taylor Exp. Taylor series approximate within its radius of convergence a function by a polynomial.

title: Power Method
comment: Power Method — Power iterations converge to the leading eigenvector of a matrix. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_iteration
alt_text: Power Method. Power iterations converge to the leading eigenvector of a matrix.

title: Advection
comment: Advection — Diffeomorphisms (warpings) are conveniently described in a Lagrangian way by advecting particles along a flow field. The Eulerian description corresponds to the advection equation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advection
alt_text: Advection. Diffeomorphisms (warpings) are conveniently described in a Lagrangian way by advecting particles along a flow field. The Eulerian description corresponds to the advection equation.

title: Nurbs
comment: Nurbs — Rational Bezier curves generalize Bernstein approximation using weights. Enables the approximation of arbitrary quadric (such as circles). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-uniform_rational_B-spline
alt_text: Nurbs. Rational Bezier curves generalize Bernstein approximation using weights. Enables the approximation of arbitrary quadric (such as circles).

title: Roots Poly
comment: Roots Poly — Interpolating linearly polynomials of a fixed degree defines an interpolation between their roots. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vieta%27s_formulas
alt_text: Roots Poly. Interpolating linearly polynomials of a fixed degree defines an interpolation between their roots.

title: Flattening
comment: Flattening — One can map a surface to a sphere by minimizing a Dirichlet energy. https://www.numerical-tours.com/matlab/meshdeform_2_parameterization_sphere
alt_text: Flattening. One can map a surface to a sphere by minimizing a Dirichlet energy.

title: Gauss Luca
comment: Gauss Luca — Gauss-Luca theorem shows that the roots of the derivative of a polynomial belong to the convex hull of the roots of the polynomial. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauss%E2%80%93Lucas_theorem
alt_text: Gauss Luca. Gauss-Luca theorem shows that the roots of the derivative of a polynomial belong to the convex hull of the roots of the polynomial.

title: Lloyd

title: Legendre Fast
comment: Legendre Fast — The Legendre transform can be approximated in O(n log(n)) using a Gaussian convolution. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendre_transformation
alt_text: Legendre Fast. The Legendre transform can be approximated in O(n log(n)) using a Gaussian convolution.

title: Marching Cube
comment: Marching Cube — The marching squares/cubes is the standard algorithm to extract iso-curves/surfaces from a discretized image/volume. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_squares
alt_text: Marching Cube. The marching squares/cubes is the standard algorithm to extract iso-curves/surfaces from a discretized image/volume.

title: Marden Thm
comment: Marden Thm — Marden theorem states that the roots of P'' are the focal point of the Steiner ellipse (largest enclosed ellipse in area) of the triangle formed by the roots of P. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marden%27s_theorem
alt_text: Marden Thm. Marden theorem states that the roots of P'' are the focal point of the Steiner ellipse (largest enclosed ellipse in area) of the triangle formed by the roots of P.

title: Divergence Dual Norm
comment: Divergence Dual Norm — Comparing probability distributions: Csiszar f-divergences measure "vertical" displacement of mass, whereas dual norm of smooth functions rather measure "horizontal" displacements. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-divergence
